title: Blueprint verb family: add, list, remove, upgrade
description: A `rcf blueprint` verb family provides the primary operator seat for composing blueprints onto a project. Every verb runs against the current tree, is idempotent where the semantics allow, and writes to the manifest's `blueprints[]` registry so the applied set is greppable and mechanical.
iWant: to add, list, remove and upgrade blueprints against my project tree from a single `rcf blueprint` verb family
soThat: composition is a first-class action instead of a one-shot init flag, and I can layer several blueprints across the life of a project without hand-editing the manifest

acceptanceCriteria.description: `rcf blueprint add <slug>` on a project with no blueprints applied writes an entry into `manifest.blueprints[]` and prints the applied slug and version
acceptanceCriteria.given: a validated project tree with no existing `blueprints[]` entries and a resolvable blueprint slug
acceptanceCriteria.then: the manifest gains one `blueprints[]` entry (slug, version, appliedAt, source, and any contributions[] the blueprint wrote), and stdout names the slug and applied version

acceptanceCriteria.description: `rcf blueprint list` prints every applied blueprint (slug, version, appliedAt) in apply order
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project with one or more blueprints already applied
acceptanceCriteria.then: every applied blueprint prints, one per line, ordered by `appliedAt`, with slug, version and apply timestamp columns

acceptanceCriteria.description: `rcf blueprint remove <slug>` removes the manifest entry and refuses when any project-authored doc references a contributed id
acceptanceCriteria.given: a project with the blueprint applied and no project-authored doc referencing any of the contributions[] ids
acceptanceCriteria.then: the `blueprints[]` entry is dropped from the manifest; when a project-authored doc DOES reference a contribution, the verb exits non-zero and prints the referencing id + path without mutating the manifest

acceptanceCriteria.description: `rcf blueprint add <slug>` is idempotent: repeating on an already-applied clean slug is a no-op with a friendly message
acceptanceCriteria.when: `rcf blueprint add <slug>` runs again with no conflicts to surface
acceptanceCriteria.then: the manifest is not rewritten, exit code is 0, and stdout names the slug as already applied at the applied version

acceptanceCriteria.description: `rcf --help` lists `blueprint` alongside the other top-level commands
acceptanceCriteria.then: the top-level usage advertises `blueprint <verb>` as an available command
